SUMMARIZER

ScoreReady

Two ways it can summarize

With a language model connected, the summarizer writes a new, shorter passage of about a quarter of the original length. The result is rejected if it contains a number that was not in your text, which guards against invented figures.

Without a model, it produces an extractive summary: it scores each sentence by how many of the passage’s frequent content words it contains, gives a small bonus to the opening sentence and to sentences with figures, and keeps the top 30 percent word for word. Nothing is reworded, so nothing can be misstated, but the sentences may not flow as smoothly.

Getting a summary you can rely on

A summary is only as good as its source. Remove menus, captions and reference lists before you paste. For anything you will quote or act on, read the summary against the original once; a tool can miss the one sentence that mattered most to you.

WORTH KNOWING

Questions and answers.

How long is the summary?

About a quarter of the original with a model, or roughly 30 percent of the sentences with offline rules. Passages of one or two sentences are returned unchanged.

Can it summarize a PDF?

Yes, if the PDF contains real text. Use Upload to open it; the text is extracted on your device. Scanned PDFs are images and cannot be read.

Does it work in Hindi?

The offline summary works in any language because it selects existing sentences. Quality is best in English, where common filler words are ignored when scoring sentences.

Will it make up facts?

Offline summaries cannot, because they only select sentences you wrote. Model summaries are checked for new numbers but can still misstate a point, so read them against the source.
